privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.body:
This page describes what information is processed when you visit thekanjo.com, the website for The Kanjo, a video game in development published by Daineku ([daineku.com](https://daineku.com/)). It covers only what this site actually does.

## What this site is

An information site about a game in development: a short description, footage, development updates and links to our channels. There are no visitor accounts, no purchases and no forms that ask for personal details.

## Server request data

Like every website, this one is served by a hosting provider that processes the technical data a browser sends with each request — your IP address, browser type, the page requested and the time. That data is used to deliver the pages and to keep the service secure and reliable. It is not used to build a profile of you.

## Cookies and tracking

The public site sets no cookies of its own and runs no analytics, tracking pixels or advertising systems.

The administration area used to edit this site is restricted to authorised editors. Signing in to it sets an authentication session cookie; nothing about ordinary visitors is stored there.

## Embedded services

Some parts of the site are provided by third parties, and using them means those parties process data under their own privacy policies:

- **YouTube.** Videos are shown as a still image until you press play. Only then is YouTube's player loaded, through youtube-nocookie.com.
- **TikTok.** Recent clips are shown through TikTok's official creator embed, which loads as you scroll to it. TikTok may set cookies and collect data when its embed loads.
- **Patreon.** Development-log entries are read by our server from Patreon's public API and shown here. Viewing this site sends nothing about you to Patreon; following a link to Patreon is governed by Patreon's own policies.

## Images and media

Images on this site may be delivered from Cloudflare's network, which processes request data in order to serve them.

## External links

Links to other sites — our channels, the publisher's site, stores — lead to services we do not control. Their privacy practices are their own.

## Content editing

The site's content is stored with a hosting database provider and edited by authorised people at Daineku. It contains no visitor data.

## Changes

This page will be updated if the site starts doing something it does not do today. The date at the top is the date of the current version.

## Contact

Questions about this page can be raised through the publisher's site, [daineku.com](https://daineku.com/).

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.body:
These are the terms on which thekanjo.com, the website for The Kanjo, is made available by its publisher, Daineku ([daineku.com](https://daineku.com/)). By using the site you accept them.

## Use of the site

The site exists to share information about The Kanjo, a video game currently in development. You may browse it, link to it and share its public pages. You may not misuse it — for example by attempting to access the administration area, interfering with its operation, or reproducing its assets as though they were your own.

## Development information

Everything shown here describes a game that is still being made. Features, mechanics, screenshots, footage, vehicles, locations and interface details may change or be removed before release, and nothing on this site is a commitment that any of them will appear in a finished product.

**No release date, platform, price or store availability is confirmed unless it has been officially announced by Daineku.** Where the site says something is not yet announced, it is not yet announced.

## Intellectual property

The Kanjo, its name, logos, artwork, screenshots, footage, text and design belong to Daineku and are protected by copyright and trademark law. They are shown here for information. You may share them in the ordinary way — a screenshot in a post, a link to a page — but you may not use them commercially, present them as your own, or use them to suggest an association with Daineku that does not exist.

## Third-party marks and services

YouTube, TikTok, Patreon, Steam and other names and marks that appear on this site belong to their respective owners. Their appearance here indicates where The Kanjo can be found or followed and does not imply any endorsement of, or by, those companies. Content embedded from those services is provided under their own terms.

## External links

The site links to other websites. Daineku does not control them and is not responsible for their content, availability or practices.

## Availability

The site is provided as it is. It may be changed, be unavailable for a time, or be withdrawn, without notice. Daineku does not guarantee that it will be uninterrupted or free of errors.

## Changes to these terms

These terms may be updated. The date at the top is the date of the current version; continued use of the site after a change means acceptance of the updated terms.

_README: THE KANJO LOADER — two cars trading position on a night highway.
THE VEHICLES ARE THE OWNER'S FINAL ART. carA is the EG6 (near lane), carB is
the EK9 (far lane, the one that closes and overtakes first). Both are derived
from IMAGES/ by `npm run assets:prepare`: trimmed to their opaque bounds so
the bottom edge of each image IS its wheel line, which is what the lane
markers are positioned against. Width and height are the trimmed pixel sizes
and are what stop the loader reflowing as the images decode.
The road, the lane markers and the light accents are drawn in CSS. Nothing is
baked into the car images, so they can be swapped without touching the
highway.
TIMING. minimumDisplayMs is a floor so a warm cache does not turn the entrance
into a flicker; one full overtake takes about 3s, so ~2200 shows a complete
trade of position. maximumDisplayMs is the ESCAPE PATH: past it the site opens
whatever is still loading. The maximum always wins if the two disagree.
WHAT 'READY' MEANS: hydration plus the display font. NOT every asset on the
page — a loader that waits for the hero image is a loader a slow connection
can hold open for a minute.
intensity: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'. A phone automatically runs one step
below whatever is set here, and prefers-reduced-motion replaces the whole
sequence with a still frame and a short fade.

_comment: V1 LANDING PAGE — deliberately short.
The order is the experience: THE KANJO, what it is, watch it, read the
development log. Four blocks and a footer, over a loader. A visitor should
be able to take the whole site in without deciding to.
EVERY BLOCK THE LONGER PAGE CARRIED STILL EXISTS. Features, development
status, the screenshot gallery, the local-video block and the links panel
are all still in the registry and still configurable — they are switched
off below. Turning one back on is `published: true` and an `order`; it is
not a code change. Nothing was deleted, and nothing extra is on the page.
COPY STATUS: anything containing the word PLACEHOLDER is NOT RENDERED — see
lib/content/placeholder.ts. A section with unwritten copy shows less rather
than showing an instruction to the site's owner. The inventory of what is
still needed is docs/CONTENT_REQUIRED.md.

_README: HERO MEDIA. hero.png is the approved 6336x2688 source, copied byte for byte by
`npm run assets:prepare`. It is never regenerated: framing is object-position
only. The red car sits right of centre (x 47-88% of the frame), so the phone
crop is pulled to 72% to keep it in view; the desktop crop sits slightly low
so the road and the tail lights carry the bottom third under the logo.
identity: 'logo' shows the supplied logo artwork as the visible identity. The
H1 is still THE KANJO — it is the logo's alt text — so a crawler and a screen
reader get the name. 'text' sets the title in the display face instead.
treatment: 'dim' (canon default) | 'strong_dim' | 'transparent' | 'blackout'.

_comment: THE PROJECT DESCRIPTION. Not a marketing section: one heading and two short
paragraphs. `blocks` is an ordered list rendered after `body` — text blocks
and YouTube blocks (the same click-to-load facade as the main video), so a
clip can sit between paragraphs later. Managed in the admin (INTRO panel).
ornament 'divider' draws the supplied brand divider above the heading. It is
used here ONCE; the badge is used once on the development log. Neither is
repeated on every section.

config.heading: ONE LOOP, AFTER DARK
config.body:
The Kanjo is a racing game built around a single elevated expressway loop at night — a fictionalised Japanese night circuit, loosely inspired rather than reproduced.

Handling aims at believable vehicle behaviour rather than simulation for its own sake, and the interface stays deliberately minimal: the road, the traffic, and the car.

_comment: THE LATEST YOUTUBE VIDEO — resolved automatically, not pinned.
THERE IS NO VIDEO YET, AND THE BLOCK HIDES ITSELF: fallback 'hide' means that
without a YOUTUBE_API_KEY (or a pinned video) nothing renders — no empty
frame, no button pointing at an empty channel. The channel is still in the
rail. The moment a key is added in Vercel, or a video is pinned in the admin,
the block appears with no code change and no deploy of its own.
mode 'latest' resolves the channel's newest PUBLIC upload server-side:
@thekanjo -> channels.list(forHandle) -> uploads playlist ->
playlistItems.list -> newest usable item
search.list is deliberately NOT used. See lib/youtube/client.ts.
mode 'pinned' + `video` keeps one specific upload on the homepage instead,
and needs no API key at all. Do not invent a video id.
TIKTOK — the official Creator Profile Embed for @the_kanjo.
It shows a selection of the profile's recent videos and needs NO TikTok
developer app, no Login Kit review and no video.list authorisation,
because the profile is public and it is ours.
Nothing is scraped, nothing is proxied, and no TikTok video is downloaded
or re-hosted. The embed markup is CONSTRUCTED by our own component from a
validated handle — TikTok HTML is never accepted from this file.
embed.js is loaded once, only when the section approaches the viewport, so
it never competes with the loader or the hero.
If TikTok is blocked or slow the block shows FOLLOW ON TIKTOK instead —
that link is the embed's own initial content, not an error state.
The upgrade path to custom The Kanjo-styled cards is the TikTok Display
API (user.info.basic + video.list) and is NOT needed for V1. See
docs/TIKTOK.md.
PATREON / DEVELOPMENT LOG.
The feed comes from the official Patreon API v2 (campaigns.posts), fetched
SERVER-SIDE. There is no credential in this file and there must never be
one: the token lives in PATREON_ACCESS_TOKEN in the server environment.
See docs/PATREON.md.
WITH NO CREDENTIALS CONFIGURED — the normal state of a fresh clone — this
renders its copy and the CTA, which is what `fallback: 'cta'` means. Set it
to 'hide' to drop the block entirely instead.
showLockedPosts lists members-only posts as title + date + MEMBERS + a link.
Their bodies are NEVER rendered whatever this is set to — the excerpt is
derived from post content only when Patreon marks the post public.
campaignUrl is empty until the owner supplies the real creator page. The
section says so rather than linking somewhere invented.

_README: VIDEOS. Two reservations, both published:false, so neither renders and no
fabricated footage ships. Bring ONE live and it becomes the featured video
under the hero.
A LOCAL CLIP (provider 'file') — preferred for gameplay and cinematics,
because it ships no third-party script and no cookies:
1. export to public/media/video/ (MP4 always; WebM as well if you can)
2. export a poster frame to the same folder — MANDATORY
3. put the MP4 in `ref` and the WebM in `sources`, WebM first in
preference order
4. set "published": true
The page shows only the poster until the visitor presses PLAY; the video file
is not fetched before that. The native <video> element handles playback,
controls, fullscreen and Picture-in-Picture — no player library.
AN EXTERNAL CLIP (provider 'youtube' or 'vimeo'):
`ref` is the BARE ID, not a watch URL — 'dQw4w9WgXcQ', not
'https://youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ&list=...'. The embed URL is
composed by the site, so a pasted URL cannot smuggle in a playlist, an
autoplay parameter or a tracking string. A poster is still mandatory, and
the provider's script only loads once somebody presses PLAY.
See docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md for resolution, duration, codec, bitrate and
whether to strip the audio track.

videos._note: An external alternative, for when a trailer lives on YouTube. `ref` is the bare id.

_README: SCREENSHOTS. Six reservations, all published:false, so none of them render
and no fabricated image ships. To bring one live:
1. export the capture to public/media/screenshots/ using the name below
2. write a real `alt` describing what is actually in the frame
3. set "published": true
That is the whole workflow. No component is edited, and `npm run test:media`
lists exactly which files are still missing.
`width`/`height` are the REAL pixel dimensions and are mandatory — they are
what reserves the image's space before it loads, so a wrong value shifts the
layout. 1920x1080 is the recommended export; see docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md for
format, quality and the night-scene pitfalls that matter for this game.
KEEP THE SET AT ONE ASPECT RATIO. The grid reserves each cell from the
entry's own dimensions, so mixed ratios give a ragged grid — it will not
shift, but it will not read as a press set either.
`order` controls position; `featured` is available for later use and is not
read by the current layout. The filenames below are suggestions, not
requirements — the path in `image.src` is the only thing that must match.

links._comment: Addressed by id from a section's config. available:false renders the block disabled with unavailableReason shown, which is the canon's behaviour for a locked row: visible, focusable, not submittable. Nothing here invents a destination.
